finding.title: Split the four >400-line hand-written files in core/sync/ (AG-3)
finding.why: Line counts: firestore_gateway.dart 408, firestore_gateway_impl.dart 1216, pull_pipeline.dart 447, sync_orchestrator.dart 1557 -- all over AG-3's 400-line cap for hand-written files. sync_orchestrator.dart alone mixes pull orchestration, status derivation, listener lifecycle, connectivity handling, identity-mismatch handling and outbox draining in one class; firestore_gateway_impl.dart carries 20+ push methods plus 6 read/listen helper families. Routine changes (this file's own history shows a new push method or channel added almost every wave) require loading the whole file's context first.
finding.recommendation: Extract SyncOrchestratorImpl's outbox-status derivation (_recomputeOutboxStatus / _skipPullOnIdentityMismatch / _maybeReviveIdentityDeadLetters) into a separate collaborator; split FirestoreGatewayImpl's per-entity push methods into smaller per-domain mixins/extensions.
acceptance_criteria: A tool/ line-count Rule-0 checker enforces the 400-line cap on hand-written .dart files (generated exempt) and lists violators with counts; these 4 files pass or carry a stated, reviewed exception.

finding.title: Remove the dead no-op catchError in OutboxPushPipeline._runValue
finding.why: `removed` is the same Future as `ourSlot`, which is built via `.then<void>((_) {}, onError: (Object _) {})` -- the onError handler there already converts any failure into a normal completion, so ourSlot/removed can never complete with an error. The later `unawaited(removed.catchError((_) {}))` is defensive code guarding against something that cannot happen.
finding.recommendation: Delete the no-op catchError call, or add a one-line comment if there's a reason (e.g. future-proofing against a refactor) to keep it.
acceptance_criteria: Line removed, or a comment explains why an unreachable catchError is intentionally retained.

finding.title: Split the 4 oversized core/sync test files back under the 400-line AG-3 cap

evidence.quote: /// Unit tests for [OutboxPushPipeline] — the concrete PushPipeline that

finding.why: firestore_gateway_impl_test.dart is 2039 lines (5.1x the cap), codecs_and_mergers_test.dart 1298, push_pipeline_impl_test.dart 1295, sync_orchestrator_test.dart 1111 — all hand-written, none generated. Per AG-3's own rationale, content past a typical agent read window is invisible, so an agent asked to update e.g. FirestoreGatewayImpl and its test can miss a group it didn't load and duplicate a helper or case that already exists further down (as happened here: pushLedgerEntriesBatch's undersized test sits ~1000 lines from pushCompletionsBatch's, with no visible cross-check). push_pipeline_impl_test.dart's bloat is largely mechanical: ~17 near-identical 'pushX -> gateway.pushX' tests (lines 462-704) differing only in method name and payload shape — a table-driven rewrite would cut several hundred lines on its own.
finding.recommendation: Split each file along its existing numbered/grouped sections (firestore_gateway_impl_test.dart's 16 groups map cleanly to ~4 files by concern: path-building+writes, batch/pagination, listeners, errors/misc); for push_pipeline_impl_test.dart, replace the per-collection routing group with one data-driven test iterating a {method, payload} table.
acceptance_criteria: find test/core/sync -name '*_test.dart' | xargs wc -l reports all 4 files at or under 400 lines

finding.title: Move codecs_and_mergers_test.dart's two suites to their AG-5-mirrored paths under test/core/sync/codec/ and test/core/sync/merge/

evidence.quote: ///   - [UiPreferencesMerger] LWW gate, per-field writes, cross-profile isolation,

finding.why: This one file tests two unrelated source files — lib/core/sync/codec/stage_definition_codec.dart and lib/core/sync/merge/ui_preferences_merger.dart — at neither of their AG-5-mirrored paths. test/core/sync/codec/ doesn't exist at all despite lib/core/sync/codec/ holding 15 codec files; test/core/sync/merge/ already exists (mergers_test.dart, drift_merge_store_test.dart) but doesn't hold ui_preferences_merger_test.dart either. The repo additionally carries a second, non-mirroring test/sync/ tree (test/sync/merge/*_roundtrip_test.dart, test/sync/codec_rules_contract_test.dart) that also touches stage_definition_codec.dart at a different (DB-integration) layer, so an agent grepping for 'where is the StageDefinitionCodec test' has to check three locations before finding this one.
finding.recommendation: Split into test/core/sync/codec/stage_definition_codec_test.dart and test/core/sync/merge/ui_preferences_merger_test.dart, each mirroring its lib/ counterpart 1:1.
acceptance_criteria: stage_definition_codec_test.dart exists at test/core/sync/codec/ and ui_preferences_merger_test.dart exists at test/core/sync/merge/

finding.title: Fix the self-referential SY-3 timeout-message assertion in sync_orchestrator_test.dart — it never calls SyncOrchestratorImpl

evidence.quote:
const message = 'Sync timed out — tap to retry';
      expect(message, contains('timed out'));

finding.why: The test declares its own local `message` string literal and asserts it contains 'timed out' — guaranteed true by the literal it just wrote — then compares a bare TimeoutException.toString() against that same local constant. It never touches SyncOrchestratorImpl or its catch block, so it provides zero protection for the orchestrator's actual TimeoutException-handling path. A maintainer reading this file alone would believe SY-3's friendly-timeout-message behavior is covered right here. Genuine end-to-end coverage of the same behavior does exist, but in a different file (test/sync/sy3_sync_error_message_sanitize_test.dart, outside this batch) — this copy is dead weight that would mask a real gap if that sibling file were ever trimmed or moved.
finding.recommendation: Delete this test (real coverage lives in test/sync/sy3_sync_error_message_sanitize_test.dart) or rewrite it to call orchestrator.pullOnLaunch() with a TimeoutException-throwing fake gateway and assert on the emitted SyncStatusError.message, matching the pattern used two tests above it in this same file.
acceptance_criteria: Test either removed with the reason in the commit message (TQ-7) or rewritten to drive pullOnLaunch() through a timeout-throwing fake gateway and assert the resulting SyncStatusError.message
